official.status_note: HKUST's online application system for 2027/28 entry opened on 2 October 2026; the Priority Round deadline for applicants with international qualifications is 25 November 2026, rolling applications run from 26 November 2026, offers are announced from late December 2026 and applications close on 30 June 2027. HKUST states all applicants are considered for academic scholarships and no separate application is required.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Successful awardees receive a full tuition waiver, renewable for normal duration of study, subject to satisfactory academic performance. HKUST's Fees and Scholarships page publishes the 2027/28 non-local tuition fee at HKD 260,000 per academic year, which is what the waiver covers. A top-up scholarship may be offered by the School/Program Office provided that the maximum limit of "Full Tuition Fee + HK$65,000 allowance" p.a. is not exceeded.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form to fill in: your HKUST undergraduate admission application is the application, and applicants from nationalities HKUST treats as underrepresented are considered automatically, with the decision normally arriving alongside your offer. The award waives the full non-local tuition of HKD 260,000 per academic year for 2027/28 entry and is renewable across the degree as long as your academic performance stays satisfactory, but it pays nothing towards living costs, so you still need to fund roughly HKD 65,000 a year of personal expenses plus accommodation on your own. Because the top-up a School or Programme Office can add is capped at full tuition plus HK$65,000, the realistic ceiling on total support is about HKD 325,000 a year, and it is discretionary rather than promised. Apply by the 25 November 2026 Priority Round if you can, since later applicants are handled on a rolling basis from 26 November.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-local applicants to HKUST undergraduate programmes who hold a nationality HKUST treats as underrepresented and want a renewable full tuition waiver without a separate scholarship application.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is on HKUST's underrepresented list before relying on this award, since the automatic consideration is nationality-based
Have a complete undergraduate admission application ready to submit before 25 November 2026 to land the Priority Round
Check the General, School/Programme-specific and English Language Admissions Requirements for your chosen programme and sit the required tests early
Budget independently for living costs: HKUST publishes roughly HKD 65,000 a year in personal expenses plus accommodation of HKD 21,000-51,000 per residential year for non-local students
Keep your grades up once enrolled, because renewal depends on satisfactory academic performance
common_rejection_risks: Assuming a separate scholarship application exists and therefore never having the admission application assessed properly - the admission application is the scholarship application
Holding a nationality that is not on HKUST's underrepresented list, in which case this particular award will not apply even though other admissions scholarships may
Missing the English Language Admissions Requirements, which are assessed at admission alongside the scholarship decision
Letting academic performance slip after enrolment, since the waiver is only renewable subject to satisfactory performance
Claiming local status you cannot support with identity documents, which HKUST warns can cancel an offer
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The waiver covers tuition only. For 2027/28 HKUST publishes roughly HKD 65,000 per academic year in personal expenses for non-local students, university accommodation of HKD 21,000-51,000 per residential year, and off-campus accommodation of HKD 4,500-18,000 per month after the first year; all of that, plus travel and insurance, is self-funded.
document_audit: Identity documents supporting your local/non-local status must match your application exactly, because discrepancies can cancel the offer
Because the scholarship rides on the admission application, any missing admission document (transcripts, predicted results, test scores) delays the scholarship decision too
No scholarship-specific document is required, so do not delay submission while preparing one
alerts: The top-up figure on HKUST's current page is HK$65,000, not HK$60,000 as still recorded in the catalogue - use the live page figure
The Priority Round deadline is 25 November 2026; from 26 November applications are handled on a rolling basis and competition for places tightens
The waiver is tuition-only and renewal is conditional on satisfactory academic performance, so it is not a guaranteed four-year entitlement
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the HKUST undergraduate admission application through the University's online application system, meet the Priority Round deadline where possible, then wait for the offer and scholarship decision, which arrive together.
